svg.aria-label: Hole-by-hole breadboard map for Pico 2 W, OLED and TSOP38238
svg.text: Column 1 on the left (numbers printed on the board). USB hangs off that end. Unplug USB while inserting parts. Each numbered column is one metal strip on that side of the trench.
Blue holes = Pico pins. Yellow = a jumper or component lead. Red hole f1 = 5 V, leave empty.
centre trench — insulator. Pico bridges it like a DIP chip.
typical Pi Hut order — if labels differ, keep a23–a26 and move the four wires
Push the Pico across the trench, USB off the left. 20 pins
in row e, 20 pins in row f, one pin per numbered column.
e1 = pin 1 GP0 f1 = pin 40 VBUS (empty)
f17 = pin 24 GP18 f20 = pin 21 GP16
Two short jumpers under the Pico, then join the long rails:
black bottom GND col 34 → top GND col 34
Leave f1 empty. That pin is 5 V from USB.
f–j in column 17 are already joined to Pico GP18.
f–j in column 19 are already joined to Pico GP17.
f–j in column 20 are already joined to Pico GP16.
Columns 32–63 of a full-size board stay empty.
2. OLED — pins in a23 a24 a25 a26
Four pins in row a. Screen hangs off the top of the board.
GND a24 → top GND rail (short black)
e25 is the same column as OLED SCL. g19 is GP17.
3. TSOP — legs in c28 c29 c30
Rounded lens toward you (toward the trench). Left to
right with the lens facing you: OUT, GND, VS.
OUT d28 → g17 (orange, crosses trench, to GP18)
VS 100Ω from top +3V3 down into a30
a31 → top GND rail (returns both capacitors)
Do not add extra links between columns 28, 29 and 30.
Before you plug USB back in
• Pico straddles the trench, USB on the left
• f1 is empty (no 5 V on the rails)
• OLED VCC and the 100Ω come from +3V3, not VBUS
• 4.7µF stripe is in column 31, plus in 30
• TSOP lens is not buried against the Pico
• Point a 38 kHz TV remote at the lens
Power is the Pico USB cable. No battery.
Later player boards use GP10–GP13 for receivers.
